cards.title: What is Spring Boot?
cards.content:
Spring Boot is an extension of the Spring framework that simplifies the bootstrapping and development of new Spring applications.

Key features include:

  • Auto-configuration: Automatically configures Spring beans based on class-path dependencies.
  • Embedded Servers: No need to deploy WAR files to external servers like Tomcat or Jetty; they are embedded.
  • Starter POMs: Simplified dependency management using opinionated starter packages.

cards.title: Inversion of Control (IoC) & Dependency Injection (DI)
cards.content:
At the core of Spring is the IoC Container, which manages the lifecycle, configuration, and assembly of objects (Beans).

Instead of manually creating objects using new, you let the container inject dependencies:

@Service
public class UserService {
    private final UserRepository userRepository;

    @Autowired
    public UserService(UserRepository userRepository) {
        this.userRepository = userRepository;
    }
}

cards.title: Understanding Spring Boot Starters
cards.content:
Starters are a set of convenient dependency descriptors that you can include in your application. They provide a one-stop-shop for all the Spring and related technologies you need, without having to hunt through sample code and copy-paste loads of dependency descriptors.

For instance, if you want to get started using Spring and JPA for database access, include the spring-boot-starter-data-jpa dependency in your project.

cards.title: Spring Bean Scopes
cards.content:
A Bean Scope defines the lifecycle and visibility of a bean within the Spring Container.

  • Singleton: (Default) Only one instance per Spring IoC container.
  • Prototype: A new instance is created every time the bean is requested.
  • Request: A single instance per HTTP request (Web-aware only).
  • Session: A single instance per HTTP session (Web-aware only).

cards.title: Configuration & Profiles
cards.content:
Spring Boot externalizes configurations using properties or YAML files (application.properties or application.yml).

You can dynamically change configurations using Profiles (e.g., dev, prod):

# application-dev.properties
server.port=8081

# application-prod.properties
server.port=80

Access values using the @Value annotation or @ConfigurationProperties.

cards.title: Actuator & DevTools
cards.content:
Spring Boot includes developer tools and production-ready monitoring utilities:

  • DevTools: Enables features like automatic restarts upon source change and LiveReload.
  • Actuator: Exposes production-ready HTTP/JMX endpoints to monitor and interact with your application.

Useful Actuator endpoints include /actuator/health, /actuator/metrics, and /actuator/env.

content.text: To verify if your application is healthy using Spring Boot Actuator, you send a GET request to the path: /actuator/[blank].

cards.title: Spring Boot Architecture Layers
cards.content:
Spring Boot encourages a clean separation of concerns using a standard 3-layer architecture:

  • Presentation Layer: Rest Controllers handling incoming HTTP requests.
  • Business Layer: Service classes where business rules are applied.
  • Data Access Layer: Repositories mapping database logic to Java entities.
